assumptions: Took the issue's recommended fix shape rather than the alternative: kept the engine's `DesignPipelineInput.noFreshen` / `noFill` contract exactly as-is (design-pipeline/index.ts:55 and :90 still skip a phase only on `=== true`) and corrected only the command layer's option read. The defect is at the command boundary; the engine contract is coherent and is consumed by tests and callers beyond this command. The decisive constraint, added in round 2: `noFreshen` and `noFill` are fields of the PUBLISHED MCP inputSchema for `run_design_pipeline` (mcp/tools/design-pipeline.ts:32-33), so renaming them would break an external tool surface with unknown clients, or force a translation layer that reintroduces the same double negative at a second boundary.

Used `opts.freshen === false` / `opts.fill === false` rather than a truthiness check (`!opts.freshen`). Empirically verified against the exact commander in use (12.1.0, resolved at packages/cli/node_modules/commander): Commander ALWAYS populates `freshen`/`fill`, defaulting both to `true`, so only an explicit `false` distinguishes 'flag passed' from 'flag absent'. A `=== undefined` test would never fire. Round 2 re-probed this across 15 argv shapes — bare run, each flag alone, both together, the flag passed twice, the flag after the `--` terminator, and adjacent to the variadic `--files` — and `freshen`/`fill` are own properties on every one. The positive forms `--freshen` and `--no-freshen=false` throw `commander.unknownOption`, so there is no third state. This also preserves the command's established contract of OMITTING unsupplied flags from the input rather than sending `false` for them.

Also corrected the `DesignPipelineCliOptions` interface (`noFreshen?`/`noFill?` -> `freshen`/`fill`). This is part of the same root cause, not scope creep: the interface asserted a shape Commander never produces, which is precisely why the inert reads typechecked cleanly and the bug survived review. Leaving it would let the same defect be reintroduced silently. Review round 2 additionally dropped the `?` from both fields (design-pipeline.ts:43-44) so the type mirrors runtime reality. CORRECTION within round 2: an earlier revision of this file claimed the `?` removal closed the hole, i.e. that it made an `=== undefined` read fail to compile. It does not. TypeScript exempts `=== undefined` from its no-overlap check (TS2367), so `opts.freshen === undefined` compiles clean against `boolean` exactly as against `boolean | undefined` — verified with `tsc --strict` on a minimal repro and against this package's own tsconfig. The `.action()` callback is typed `(...args: any[])` in commander's typings, so the annotation is never structurally checked either. The change is honest documentation with zero compiler enforcement; what actually guards the dead read is the mirrored pair of tests. The interface is local to design-pipeline.ts and used only as the `.action()` parameter type — no object-literal construction exists anywhere in the repo.

INVERTED AN EXISTING PASSING TEST. At the pre-fix revision (c7bdb08c6~1), packages/cli/tests/commands/design-pipeline-command.test.ts:140-172 was a deliberate CHARACTERIZATION block that pinned the BROKEN behavior (asserting the input does NOT contain `noFreshen`/`noFill`). Those three assertions now assert the opposite. This is intended: the original block's own comment stated 'These tests will go red the moment it lands, which is exactly the signal wanted.' A reviewer must see that a previously-passing assertion changed meaning. The replacement block is at :140-205 in the current tree (both ranges quoted JSDoc-open to describe-close).

Added guard tests beyond a straight inversion, covering the over-correction: a bare run must still OMIT both keys, and each flag alone must not set the other's key. Without these, a fix keyed off key-presence rather than `=== false` would pass the inverted assertions while skipping every phase on every run. The guards pass in the pre-fix and post-fix states by design; they constrain the fix, they do not reproduce the bug. Review round 2 added the missing MIRROR half (design-pipeline-command.test.ts:201-204, '--no-fill alone must not set noFreshen'): round 1 shipped only the `--no-freshen` direction, and a mutation probe confirmed the asymmetry was load-bearing — mutating the `fill` branch to also set `input.noFreshen` survived the round-1 suite (46 passed) and fails the round-2 suite (1 failed | 46 passed of 47, failing at :203).

Held scope to design-pipeline.ts only. Two sibling instances of the identical defect class were found and deliberately NOT touched: test-craft.ts:86 (`opts.noSourcePair === true` against `.option('--no-source-pair')` at :40, tracked as issue #1882, separate lane in flight) and dashboard.ts:121 (`opts.noOpen !== true` against `.option('--no-open')` at :132, tracked as issue #1956).

Three review findings adjacent to this fix were filed as follow-ups rather than grown into this PR, which is scoped `Closes #1881`. #1958: printPipelineResult (design-pipeline.ts:112-156, render at :121-127) prints `newContext()`'s untouched `false` defaults as measurements when FRESHEN is skipped, reporting `DESIGN.md=no tokens.json=no` for a project where the files exist, with no skip marker in `--json`. #1960: with FILL skipped, `anyBootstrap` (report.ts:46) stays false and computeVerdict (report.ts:56-64) returns `pass` for a design-system-less project that reports `warn` without the flag — a false-green verdict, though not an exit-code regression since both map to 0. #1959: `--ci` is a separate, pre-existing inert flag on this same command (declared design-pipeline.ts:61, written :80, accepted at design-pipeline/index.ts:35, read by nothing; `FixInput` at phases/fix.ts:21-27 has no `ci` field), and the green test at design-pipeline-command.test.ts:104-107 reads as coverage while proving only that a value reaches a field with no readers. CORRECTION (round 2): an earlier revision claimed the first two were 'reachable only BECAUSE this fix works'. That overstates it. Both states have been reachable since `run_design_pipeline` shipped — its inputSchema declares `noFreshen`/`noFill` (mcp/tools/design-pipeline.ts:32-33) and passes the input straight to the engine at :71, and tests/design-pipeline/integration/end-to-end.test.ts:89-93 and :95-102 already exercise both. This fix makes them reachable from the CLI as well. They are pre-existing defects on a live surface, not regressions this PR introduces — which strengthens rather than weakens the case for filing them separately.
rootCause: Commander's negated-flag convention applied backwards. `.option('--no-freshen')` defines an option named `freshen` (default `true`, set to `false` when passed) and never produces a `noFreshen` key. The action read `opts.noFreshen === true` / `opts.noFill === true`, which are `undefined` on every code path, so `input.noFreshen` / `input.noFill` were never set and the engine always ran FRESHEN and FILL. Two documented flags were silently inert. FILL is both the expensive phase and the ONLY phase that writes into the adopter's repository (phases/fill.ts:98, :108, :113, :123 write or append design-system/DESIGN.md and tokens.json), so while `--no-fill` was inert there was no way to stop a bare `harness design-pipeline` from mutating the repo.
